mainTopic: Who is greater, the one who says the ברכה or the one who answers אמן, and the closing teaching that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world
overview: This last section of מסכת נזיר opens by finishing רב's advice to his son חייא: grab the chance to lead the ברכה over the cup at ברכת המזון. רב הונא gave his son רבה the same advice. The גמרא asks whether this means saying the ברכה is better than answering אמן. It points to a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says the one who answers אמן is greater, and רבי נהוראי supports him with a battlefield parable. The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this, since another ברייתא says the one who says the ברכה is rewarded first. The מסכת then ends with רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, as the פסוק in ישעיהו says. A closing הדרן line finishes the chapter הגוים אין להם נזירות and the whole of מסכת נזיר.

steps.title: Grab the chance to lead the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב tells his son חייא, and רב הונא tells his son רבה, to grab the chance to lead the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grab the chance and say the blessing. רב הונא also told his son רבה: grab the chance and say the blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: Two fathers, רב and רב הונא, both teach their sons the same thing: when there is a chance to lead the ברכה, take it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two words finish רב's instruction to his son חייא, which started just before this section. רב הונא's matching advice shows this was an accepted attitude: leading the ברכה is something to go after. That assumption is what the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.english: Grab the chance and say the blessing.
phrases.notes: This finishes what רב told his son חייא just before, about leading the ברכה over the cup at ברכת המזון.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rav Huna said to Rabba, his son:
Grab the chance and say the blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's advice from just before and adds רב הונא's matching advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is better to grab the chance to lead the ברכה yourself.

steps.title: Isn't answering amen greater than blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the advice using רבי יוסי's teaching that the one who answers אמן is greater, supported by רבי נהוראי's battle parable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean the one who says the blessing is better? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי יוסי says: the one who answers amen is greater than the one who says the blessing. And רבי נהוראי said to him: By Heaven, that is true! You can see it from war: the assistant troops start the battle, but the mighty warriors are the ones who win.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether this advice means that saying the ברכה is better than answering אמן. It then brings a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and רב הונא's advice assumes the one who says the ברכה is more important. רבי יוסי says the one who answers אמן is greater. רבי נהוראי's parable makes the point: the ברכה is like the assistant troops who open the fight, and the אמן is like the strong warriors who come after and win it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say...? (the גמרא draws a conclusion and then questions it)
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Assistant troops or camp helpers in an army

phrases.english: Is this to say that the one who says the blessing is better?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
Greater is the one who answers "amen"
than the one who says the blessing.
And Rabbi Nehorai said to him:
By Heaven! It is so:
Know this, for the assistant troops
start the battle,
and the mighty warriors win.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind the advice in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea, implied by רב and רב הונא, that saying the ברכה is better than answering אמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי, supported by רבי נהוראי, saying that answering אמן is greater than saying the ברכה. So why tell your son to grab the ברכה?
steps.confusionAlert: In the parable, the ones who start the battle (the assistants) stand for the person saying the ברכה. The ones who win (the mighty warriors) stand for the one answering אמן. Don't mix them up.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that תנאים argue about this, and a different ברייתא gives priority to the one who says the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches: both the one who says the blessing and the one who answers amen are included in the meaning, but the one who says the blessing is rushed to first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי יוסי is only one opinion, and another ברייתא disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא says both people take part in the blessing, but the one who says the ברכה is rewarded first. That opinion makes saying the ברכה greater, and רב and רב הונא's advice follows it. So their advice does not contradict every source; they simply hold like the other תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
Included in the meaning (of the פסוק)

phrases.english: It is a dispute between Tannaim, as it is taught:
Both the one who says the blessing and the one who answers "amen"
are included in the meaning,
phrases.notes: He means both count as people who bless in the פסוק that calls on the people to bless (נחמיה 9:5).

phrases.english: but they rush to the one who says the blessing first.
phrases.notes: The one who says the ברכה gets his reward first.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the advice follows a different תנא from רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of רבי יוסי, it seemed there was no basis for preferring to say the ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another ברייתא holds that the one who says the ברכה comes first, and רב and רב הונא follow that view.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether it is greater to say the ברכה or to answer אמן is a dispute between תנאים. רב and רב הונא follow the view that the one who says the ברכה comes first, so they told their sons to grab the chance.

steps.title: Torah scholars increase peace in the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, as it says: "And all your children will be taught by ה׳, and great will be the peace of your children."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: people who learn Torah bring more peace into the world. It proves this from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not part of the אמן discussion. The פסוק connects being "taught by ה׳" with "great peace," which shows that Torah learning leads to peace. It is a well-known closing line, used here to end the מסכת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
Torah scholars increase peace in the world,
as it says: "And all your children will be taught by ה׳,
and great will be the peace of your children."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים מַרְבִּים שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate teaching that closes the מסכת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world, as shown by ישעיהו 54:13.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a famous ending used to close several מסכתות, finishing the learning with a blessing of peace.
steps.whatToRemember: The מסכת ends with the message that Torah learning brings peace: תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter הגוים אין להם נזירות and finishing מסכת נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The text closes the chapter הגוים אין להם נזירות and declares that מסכת נזיר is complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter הגוים אין להם נזירות, and with this מסכת נזיר is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not a new argument. It is the closing line that ends the chapter and the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words הדרן עלך mean 'we will return to you.' They show our wish to come back and learn this chapter again. The second half, וסליקא לה מסכת נזיר, tells us this was the last chapter, so the whole מסכת is now done.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The traditional words for closing a chapter.
The status of being a נזיר
And it is finished. Used when a whole מסכת is complete.
A tractate, one full book of the גמרא

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת נזיר is now complete. It ends right after the teaching that תלמידי חכמים increase peace in the world.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
chapter "Gentiles do not have נזירות"
and מסכת נזיר is finished.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדְרָן עֲלָךְ הַגּוֹיִם אֵין לָהֶם נְזִירוּת וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter and the מסכת after the final teaching about תלמידי חכמים increasing peace.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter הגוים אין להם נזירות is closed, and the learning of מסכת נזיר is complete.
